conditions: Valid intact input database and one forward transaction
Rollback versions1, no autovacuum, current exact physical/header pages, zero reserved bytes, standard payload fractions
Fresh-key normal insertions and root creation only; no replacement/update/delete/preformatted/transfer operations
Complete count of every attempted row/index insertion, implicit index, trigger, schema and internal write; bound FULL serialized BtreePayload, never JSON length
No ATTACH/VACUUM/extensions/custom VFS/settings change, continued writing after rollback/error, or retry
Separate complete caller/native/VFS proof and held before-create capacity required
derivation: For a normal non-preformatted fresh-key sqlite3BtreeInsert, fillInCell executes at most once and balance at most once. Each table-row and each index-key insertion is a separate counted call, not one SQL statement.

With zero reserved bytes, overflow pages carry pageSize-4 payload bytes. Ignoring every local payload byte gives ceil(fullSerializedPayload/(pageSize-4)) overflow allocations. Include nZero in table payload; include the complete serialized index key.

Runtime cursor descent refuses depth >=20. Non-root balancing has a runtime NB+2=5 page guard BEFORE its allocation loop; existing siblings are reused. Charge all five output pages as allocations at 21 levels, plus a deeper-root child and a separate quick-balance page: 107 allocations per insertion. Parent traversal decreases its stack level; root deepening introduces one additional child iteration.

No-autovacuum root creation allocates one page. No pointer-map pages or relocations are allowed. Every allocation is charged TWO page-number increments to cover a pending-byte-page gap even though that gap can be crossed only once. No freelist, deletion or rollback credit is taken.

This bounds logical page count for a completely inventoried prefix, including an insertion attempt that fails. It does not establish a complete application native-operation inventory, VFS file-length/preallocation behavior, physical allocated blocks, statement journals, WAL or SQL scratch.

Capture DDL updates sqlite_schema and creates implicit indexes; its receipt insert may fire existing receipt-table triggers. Neither SQL/DDL statement counts nor the currently pinned main-journal review prove the required native insertion/root inventory. Do not use this primitive as capture writer admission.
